title: Warm Middle Eastern Cheese Curds Tagine
description: A funky and cozy Middle Eastern dish featuring cheese curds, nuka-pickle, and FODMAP-friendly ingredients, with a unique glassy-jelly texture. This dish is perfect for a cold winter night.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large clay or ceramic tagine or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until it is softened and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic-infused oil, ground cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper, and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add the chopped nuka-pickle and cook, stirring occasionally, for 2 minutes.
Add the cheese curds and chicken broth, and stir gently to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, until the cheese curds are melted and the sauce is glassy and jelly-like, about 10 minutes.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro, if desired.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
